application: Name the framework as recorded and apply only its recorded first principle: the internal model of money, worth, and possibility must end in concrete financial results. For each option, require the visible path from intention to a measurable financial outcome (a written goal, a retained amount, an ownership position) before the principle counts in the option's favor.
Where a brief offers attitude without a financial mechanism, record the principle as unapplied rather than satisfied.
items.basis_note: Framework name and first principle exactly as recorded in the Skill 22 derivative blueprint for The Wealth Choice (Sections 2, 3, and 4). The blueprint states the remaining laws live in a playbook appendix that is not part of the authorized export, so this pack asserts only the recorded first principle and does not enumerate or reconstruct a list of seven laws. The source record is an unverified derivative blueprint, not the book.
counterexamples: A founder with a confident wealth mindset and no savings mechanism, no ownership target, and no written goal fails the recorded first principle; belief has not ended in financial results.
A plan that lists seven reconstructed laws from memory would fail this pack's own standard; the framework is applied only as far as the recorded material reaches.
evidence_needed: The client's written financial goal, if one exists
The mechanism by which the option converts income or effort into retained results
The measurement that would show the principle was applied
limits: The framework is incompletely recorded: six of its seven laws are not in the material available to this pack and are never scored or paraphrased from memory.
A stated philosophy is the author's orientation, not evidence that following it causes wealth for any particular client.
Framework claims are stated as the blueprint's recorded terms, never as verified quotations from the author.
items.name: The Seven Laws of Wealth (as recorded in the blueprint)
preconditions: A decision with a financial dimension is on the table.
The brief can state, or honestly lacks, a written goal and a retention or ownership mechanism.
questions_to_ask: Where does this option end financially: what is retained, owned, or measurably different when it completes?
Is the confidence in this plan attached to a mechanism, or only to an attitude?

application: Before scoring any wealth-building option, require the three elements the blueprint's task mode records for a financial plan: a written net-worth goal, a stated minimum savings or retention rate, and a timeline for ownership income. The blueprint's template records a 10 percent minimum savings rate; the client's own rate is the client's to set.
Evaluate each option against those three elements: what it does to net worth over the horizon, what it retains, and whether it moves income from labor-only toward ownership.
Treat a missing element as missing evidence that conditions the card, not as a detail to invent.
items.basis_note: Built from the Skill 22 derivative blueprint for The Wealth Choice (Sections 7 and 8): its task mode requires the written net-worth goal, minimum savings rate, and ownership-income timeline, and its execution standard makes an explicit decision plus a written specific net-worth goal a precondition of work. Derivative blueprint, unverified quality, section locators only.
counterexamples: A high-revenue quarter with no retention and no change in what the owner owns scores as activity under this framework, however strong the revenue looks.
A modest, unglamorous purchase of equipment the business will own for a decade scores as wealth building because the accounting can point to the retained asset.
evidence_needed: Current net-worth position or an honest statement that it is unknown
The retention or savings rate the plan actually assumes
Which income in the plan is ownership income, and on what timeline
limits: This is an accounting lens for a decision, not personal financial advice; individualized investment, tax, or legal conclusions belong to qualified professionals.
Cash affordability and downside exposure are the Tiffany Aliche seat's domain; this framework asks the long-horizon ownership question and does not replace her arithmetic.
The 10 percent figure is the blueprint template's recorded parameter, reported as such; it is not prescribed to any client.
items.name: Net-worth and ownership accounting
preconditions: The decision commits money, time, or both over a horizon longer than the immediate transaction.
The client can state a net-worth goal or accept that the goal is not yet written.
questions_to_ask: What is the written net-worth goal this decision serves, and by when?
What share of the income this produces is retained, and what will be owned at the end of the timeline?

application: Before endorsing a commitment, require the written purpose statement the blueprint's execution standard records: the specific outcome, the timeline, and the value to be given in return. Score the option against that statement; a commitment that cannot be written this way is not yet a decision this seat can support.
Use the statement at review time: the outcome and timeline are the yardstick the result is measured against, not a revised story told afterward.
items.basis_note: Built from the Skill 22 derivative blueprint for What Makes the Great Great (Sections 3, 7, and 8): its mission-statement and execution standards require specific outcomes, a timeline, and the value to be given in return, inside a phased methodology whose first phase the blueprint frames in spiritual terms. That faith framing is the author's as recorded; it is reported, never imposed on a client and never treated as evidence. Derivative blueprint, unverified quality, section locators only.
counterexamples: A goal stated as growth or success, with no outcome, date, or value offered in return, fails the standard and cannot anchor a commitment.
A written statement completed after the money is spent is a rationalization, not the standard applied; the blueprint requires it before work begins.
evidence_needed: The written purpose statement, or its absence
The value the client will give in return, stated concretely
The review date at which outcome and timeline will be checked
limits: The standard disciplines commitment; it does not predict success, and a well-written statement is not evidence of demand or affordability.
The methodology's spiritual framing belongs to the author's presentation. Clients who prefer secular wording receive the same standard without it.
items.name: Written purpose and execution standard
preconditions: A commitment, plan, or mission-level decision is being considered.
The client is willing to write the intended outcome before acting.
questions_to_ask: What is the specific outcome, on what timeline, and what value will be given in return?
When will this statement be reopened and the result compared against it?

application: Classify the block before recommending: mindset (beliefs or identity limiting action), knowledge (a skill or fact is missing), action (the client knows what to do and is not doing it), or material constraint (a documented external condition). Each class has a different remedy; name the class and the evidence for the classification.
If the classification cannot be made from the brief, say which class is suspected, what would confirm it, and condition the card.
items.basis_note: Built from the assessment phases recorded in both blueprints: The Wealth Choice blueprint (Section 6) diagnoses whether the block is mindset, knowledge, or action, and the What Makes the Great Great blueprint (Sections 5 and 6) assesses a consciousness gap and the hidden payoffs of staying stuck. The fourth class, material constraint, is required by this seat's boundary in the build directive (Section 7.9) and by the Great Great blueprint's own limitation (Section 12): a methodology for succeeding within existing systems does not dissolve those systems. Derivative blueprints, unverified quality.
counterexamples: Prescribing confidence work to a client whose documented constraint is a denied credit line misclassifies the block; the remedy belongs to the constraint, not the mindset.
Prescribing more information to a client who already knows the steps and is avoiding them misclassifies an action block as a knowledge block.
evidence_needed: What the client has already tried, and what happened
Documented external conditions bearing on the decision (terms, denials, contracts, market facts)
The skill or knowledge the plan assumes, and whether it is present
limits: A classification is a working hypothesis from the brief, not a finding about a person's character or psychology.
This framework never converts a material constraint into a mindset verdict; doing so is this seat's named overreach.
items.name: Diagnose the block before prescribing
preconditions: A stalled, repeated, or underperforming effort is part of the brief.
Some record of attempts and external conditions exists, or its absence can be named.
questions_to_ask: Which is the real block here: mindset, knowledge, action, or a material constraint?
What evidence would move this classification to a different class?

application: For each option, list in two columns what the activity produces immediately (income, attention, obligations) and what endures when it ends (assets owned, equity, capability, systems, durable network value). Score the option on the second column; the first column alone never carries this seat's support.
Attach the discipline requirement: the retained-asset or capability measure, the review date, and the result that would change this seat's assessment.
Where an option is justified purely as immediate income, say so plainly and price the trade: what long-term position is being deferred, and is that deferral chosen or accidental?
items.basis_note: BlackCEO adaptation, authored for this council from the seat's owned question and expected output in the build directive (Section 7.9). It is an operating procedure for the seat, not a framework attributed to the author. The source-grounded components it draws on (written net-worth goal, ownership income, diagnosis) carry their own records in fw-net-worth-and-ownership-accounting and fw-diagnose-the-block.
counterexamples: A fully booked calendar that leaves the owner with no retained earnings, no system, and no transferable skill is activity; this test scores it as such even when revenue rises.
A slower quarter spent building an owned asset with a long useful life can outscore a busier quarter under this test; the columns, not the noise level, decide.
evidence_needed: The option's expected immediate income and obligations
The durable asset, equity, or capability retained at completion
The client's current retained position (reserves, owned assets, existing obligations)
limits: This test supplies the long-horizon ownership view; it does not override cash feasibility, legality, or customer harm, which other seats and hard constraints own.
Immediate income is sometimes the right choice, for example to protect stability; the test requires the trade to be explicit, not forbidden.
items.name: Activity versus asset test
preconditions: The seat has been given a decision brief with at least two options or an option and a status quo.
questions_to_ask: When this is finished, what will you own that you do not own now?
What measure, reviewed on what date, will show whether this built wealth or only activity?

note: Four frameworks are traced to the two Skill 22 derivative blueprints and are labeled with that basis and its limits; the blueprint for The Wealth Choice names a Seven Laws framework whose remaining laws are not in the authorized export, and this pack asserts only the recorded first principle rather than reconstructing the list. One framework is an explicit BlackCEO adaptation and is never attributed to the author.
